messages:
Sam (sales): FYI Acme POC is stuck. Private endpoint + VPC DNS; clients inside customer VPC get TLS certchain errors when calling our private endpoint. Can someone triage?
Amanda (solutions): what error are they seeing exactly? screenshot?
Sam (sales): "GET /v1/generate" fails with tls: certificate signed by unknown authority in app logs. curl -v shows 'certificate verify failed'.
Sam (sales): They also pasted stack trace and a short tcpdump showing TLS handshake stops after server Hello.
Jon (neteng): likely DNS resolution returning wrong A for the endpoint or they're hitting a proxy. Are they using AWS Interface Endpoint with Private DNS enabled?
Sam (sales): They said they created 'com.redwood-inference' interface endpoint and enabled private dns. But their infra team says they have conditional-forwarding/resolver rules to an onprem resolver.
Priya (sre): If the client resolves to our internal infra IP (10.x) we expect the cert SAN to match the public model hostname. If resolver rewrites or returns a different A, SNI mismatch can break.
Amanda (solutions): Can we get the exact FQDN they're hitting?
Sam (sales): fqdn: private-api.redwood.example (customer replaced). They said dig +short private-api.redwood.example returns 172.31.11.9 from their app host.
Jon (neteng): That IP is in their NAT pool - looks like conditional forwarder returning a CNAME to a split-hosted zone. Could be their resolver returning the NAT'd egress IP instead of the interface endpoint IP.
Priya (sre): Also, if their egress firewall forces outbound to go via proxy, OCSP stapling or full chain fetch to CA may fail. Any firewall logs?
Sam (sales): customer ran tcpdump: they see SYN->SYN/ACK with our endpoint, then ClientHello, ServerHello, then connection resets at cert send. They attached a wire capture link.
Jon (neteng): Two quick checks for them: 1) From app host: dig +short private-api.redwood.example @169.254.169.253 (or their resolver). 2) curl --resolve private-api.redwood.example:443:172.31.11.9 -v https://private-api.redwood.example/health -- This forces IP; if TLS verifies then DNS is the issue.
Amanda (solutions): Also ask them to curl with -k to confirm handshake path vs cert trust. If -k works, it's cert validation; if not, deeper handshake mismatch.
Sam (sales): I'll share both commands and the tcpdump. They ran the curl --resolve and it still failed with same cert verify error.
Priya (sre): Ok that means the IP they resolved to is presenting a cert that the app doesn't trust. Could be our edge returning a wildcard for public host but their client uses a root CA store missing new CA. What CA does their java runtime trust?
Sam (sales): It's an older distro, OpenJDK 8u202.
Jon (neteng): That can lack modern roots and OCSP access. Options: 1) Client update CA bundle. 2) Have them route DNS to our interface endpoint IP (we can provide expected private IPs per region) so the endpoint returns the correct cert chain. 3) If resolver is forced to onprem DNS, add conditional forwarder for our private hosted zone to return the endpoint IPs.
Amanda (solutions): For (2) we can provide the VPC endpoint ENI IPs but they change on scaling. Better: ensure AWS Interface Endpoint private DNS is actually returning our AWS provided hostname (com.amazonaws.vpce...).
Sam (sales): Customer says they can't change resolver due to security policy. They're requesting a short-term workaround: allowlist egress to our OCSP responder / CA distribution URL so their runtime can fetch chain.
Priya (sre): That should work. Provide list: CA issuer URL (https://ocsp.example-ca.com/), and our telemetry hosts for stapling fallback. Also ask them to allow traffic to our health and model ports (443, 8443).
Sam (sales): I'll send allowed egress IPs and domains. Any extra logging we can enable on our side to confirm connection reaching correct backend?
Jon (neteng): We can turn on connection logging for that customer endpoint and capture SNI and certificate presented. Tagging this thread when done.
InfraBot: (automated) Enabled connection debug for endpoint private-api.redwood.example in us-east-1 for customer AcmeCorp. Logs will be retained 72h.
Amanda (solutions): Great. Also add note about split-horizon DNS docs: https://intra.docs/redwood/privatelink-dns (sent link).
Sam (sales): Customer agreed to open firewall for OCSP + health endpoints and will test. I'll update once they test. :thumbsup:
Priya (sre): If they still fail after egress opens, ask for a full 'openssl s_client -connect 172.31.11.9:443 -servername private-api.redwood.example -showcerts' output and we'll inspect chain.
Sam (sales): Will do. Thanks team.
Amanda (solutions): ping @Jon and @Priya if no update in 4h.
Sam (sales): 4h reminder set.
Sam (sales): (after 2h) Customer tested egress change -> TLS now passes, app successful. They said root CA fetch fixed the chain. Marking POC blocker resolved. :tada:
Priya (sre): Nice. Please add short note to the POC summary about resolver restrictions and CA fetch requirement so next sales handoff knows the mitigation.
Sam (sales): Added to POC doc. Closing thread.
